ai.title: Freebuff CLI 0.2.4 ships server-driven model catalog and keychain auth
ai.summary: The Freebuff 0.2.4 manifest was bumped from 0.2.3 to 0.2.4, packaging the server-driven model catalog so model prices, badges, effort ladders and handles are fetched from GET /api/v1/freebuff/models instead of being compiled into the CLI. The auth token now moves from credentials.json into the OS keychain (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, Linux Secret Service via Bun.secrets) on login, with loadStoredAuthToken reading it once at startup and moveTokenToKeychain mirroring it after each write. Because only this commit carries the package.json bump while the functional members landed in the surrounding snapshot, behavior is only observable in builds that include the release members.
ai.evidence: This commit bumps the version field in freebuff/cli/release/package.json from 0.2.3 to 0.2.4. The release window members ship the server-driven model catalog (cli/src/state/freebuff-catalog-store.ts, cli/src/hooks/use-freebuff-model-catalog.ts, cli/src/utils/freebuff-model-catalog.ts), the keychain auth token migration (cli/src/utils/auth-token-store.ts, cli/src/utils/auth.ts), the catalog-root agent definition (cli/src/utils/freebuff-catalog-agent.ts, cli/src/utils/freebuff-agent-selection.ts), and the policy overlay seam (common/src/constants/freebuff-model-policy-overlay.ts).
ai.unknowns: The diff for this commit contains only the package.json bump; the catalog and keychain source hunks belong to the snapshot members, so rollout to end users depends on whether a build bundled the full release window.

eli5.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.4 introduces a server-driven model catalog so the list of free AI models, their prices, and availability can be updated without requiring a new app download, alongside moving your login token out of a plain text file and into your computer's secure keychain storage. The model picker now reflects what the server decides is available in real time, including daily session limits and promotional offers, and the app automatically uses the correct model root when a catalog is present or falls back to the older per-model roots when it is not. Your login token is now stored in the OS keychain (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, or Linux Secret Service) instead of credentials.json, with a fallback to the file if the keychain is unavailable so you are never locked out. Sessions now report richer country-verification and plan-upsell information, and a country verification prompt only appears when verifying can actually change your access. Catalog-only models are unreachable when the catalog cannot be fetched, and the app refreshes the catalog after a stale-handle error using the new handle for the same model. If you are not on Freebuff, none of this applies, since the keychain and catalog features are Freebuff-only.

ai.title: Deduplicate credentials read/parse failure logging
ai.summary: The credentials parse path in userFromJson and the read path in getUserCredentials now route errors through logCredentialsFailureOnce, which keys each failure by its message and profile so the same parse or read error is logged once per process instead of once per render, since the credentials file is re-read on every app-shell render. A new MAX_LOGGED_CREDENTIALS_FAILURES = 20 bound and a loggedCredentialsFailures Set prevent unbounded growth, and resetCredentialsFailureLogForTests is exported so the integration and keychain tests can clear the set between cases and assert that an unreadable file logs once per distinct failure rather than once per read.
ai.evidence: In cli/src/utils/auth.ts, the catch blocks of userFromJson and getUserCredentials now call a new logCredentialsFailureOnce that deduplicates by key (parse:${profileName}:${errorMessage} and read:${message}) and caps logging at MAX_LOGGED_CREDENTIALS_FAILURES = 20, replacing the previous direct logger.error calls; a new exported resetCredentialsFailureLogForTests clears the in-memory set for tests.
ai.unknowns: The unknown is the production rate at which users run multiple CLI versions against the same credentials file, which the deduplication only mitigates at the cost of one line per distinct failure rather than total silence.

ai.summary: This release bumps the Freebuff CLI manifest version from 0.2.4 to 0.2.5 in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json`, carrying forward two prior source changes. eli5.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.5 is a small update focused on keeping your login secure and cleaning up confusing messages when your free plan runs low on usage. When you sign in, the app now locks down where it stores your login file so other people on the same computer can't peek at it (it sets the file to be readable only by you), and if an older version left it more open, this version tightens it the next time you open the app. The app also used to repeat the same login error messages over and over (dozens of times per second) when something was wrong with your sign-in file, which spammed logs and slowed things down; now it logs each unique problem only once. Finally, when you hit your free daily usage cap, the screen you see is being prepped to look different for a specific situation where you need to verify your identity first (that's handled separately from the normal 'come back tomorrow' message), so the wording on screen should no longer mix up identity checks with regular usage limits. If you just use the app normally and hit your daily free limit, nothing else about the experience changes in this update. The available release evidence is incomplete for the broader identity-verification flow, so only the cleanup of repeated error logging and the tighter login file permissions are clearly confirmed as shipped behaviors.

eli5.text: The CLI now creates a unique device key for each installation and uses it to cryptographically sign every request it makes when fetching and using the model catalog. When a user's model list is fetched from the server, unopened (future-dated) models are immediately removed before the list is shown or used, so they can never be accidentally selected or run. This strengthens security for users on the new catalog mode by binding each device to its requests, but most users won't notice a difference in daily use aside from improved model list reliability; the changes are live today for installations using the server-driven catalog path.

eli5.text: This Freebuff CLI 0.2.9 release strengthens two safety and display areas. First, the terminal now strips hidden escape sequences (like OSC 52 clipboard writes and window-title changes) from all command output and AI-generated text before it is drawn, so a script or fetched page can no longer rewrite your clipboard, retitle your window, or move the cursor on screen. Second, the ad system no longer fetches ads on the landing screen when the terminal is too short to show the banner (below 18 rows), and a separate server-side change makes the command-checker used by sponsored runs refuse to execute lines it cannot fully read (deeply nested wrappers, undecodable PowerShell scripts, and script-file commands), asking the user to run those commands directly instead. Together, these changes reduce both screen hijacking and the risk that an untrusted repository's scripts can trigger an ad slot that nobody sees. Concrete highlights: a new terminal-sanitizer utility removes terminal control sequences from command output, AI tool results, and inline ad text so invisible bytes are cleaned before rendering; the landing-screen ad hook is gated to only fetch when terminal height is at least 18 rows; and the sponsored-run command walk fails closed on command lines it cannot finish reading (wrappers nested past a limit, an -EncodedCommand that will not decode, and a -File script whose contents are off the line), refusing them rather than passing them through. Everyday impact: when you view AI agent output that contains a URL, a fetched web page, or a repository's own test script, any embedded terminal escape bytes are stripped, so the visible text you read is exactly what is printed and no hidden control can alter your terminal session. On terminals shorter than 18 rows the landing screen no longer attempts to load an ad for a banner it cannot display, and when a sponsored (ad-supported) run hands the agent a command line that contains unreadable nesting, it now stops and asks you to run those commands yourself instead of executing something it cannot fully inspect.
